emptyState.title: Ask Flower
emptyState.description: Flower uses your Local AI Profile, inspects remembered environments, and prepares actions before runtimes do any read or write.
emptyState.exploreDescription: Understand what is here, what it is for, and how to get started.
emptyState.explorePrompt:
Look at the current working directory and explain in everyday language what is here, what it is for, and how I can use it.

First inspect the top-level contents and any necessary introductory documents to determine whether this is a software project, an application, a collection of reference materials, or another kind of folder.

If it is a software project, focus on the problem it solves, its main features, who it is for, and where to start. Based on the actual documentation and current environment, give me the shortest getting-started steps and one concrete usage example. Explain which prerequisites are already available and which are missing.

If it contains documents or reference materials, summarize the main content, identify the best files to read first, and suggest a reading order.

Deliver a concise usage guide. Clearly state anything uncertain rather than guessing. If the folder contains several independent projects, give an overview first and let me choose. This task is for understanding only; do not install or modify anything.
emptyState.computerDescription: Check its specifications, resource usage, and current operating condition.
emptyState.computerPrompt:
Help me understand the computer I am currently connected to with a brief system health check.

First confirm which device you are actually inspecting and whether it is local or remote. Check the operating system, processor, memory, disk capacity and free space, and current CPU, memory, and disk usage. Include graphics hardware and battery information when available.

Explain what these findings mean in everyday language, and list the few processes using the most resources right now. If you find something worth attention, provide the actual measurements, possible impact, and the most useful first step. If a single sample is insufficient to reach a conclusion, say so.

Finish with a concise report covering specifications, current condition, and points to watch. Mark information you cannot obtain, do not invent problems just to fill a recommendations list, and do not change settings or end processes.
emptyState.appsDescription: Find installed apps and tools for everyday tasks.
emptyState.appsPrompt:
Take stock of the main applications already installed on the connected device so I can understand what this computer can help me do right away.

Start with the system application list and standard installation locations. Group the apps by their actual uses, such as office work and reading, web browsing and communication, images and design, media, and development tools. Do not turn background components and internal system programs into a long, undifferentiated list.

For each main application, briefly explain what it can help me do and how to open it. Where several apps serve similar purposes, explain when each is useful. Based on the software you actually find, suggest three to five concrete tasks I could do now, such as editing a PDF, working with a spreadsheet, or trimming a video, and name the app for each.

Distinguish installed apps from apps whose usability you have confirmed, and do not promise features you cannot verify. There is no need to install or launch any software.
emptyState.organizeDescription: Understand the files and prepare a clear, practical organization plan.
emptyState.organizePrompt:
Help me make sense of the current working directory: what is in it, and how could it be organized to make things easier to find?

Start with file names, types, sizes, and the folder structure. If needed, sample a few introductory documents to summarize the main contents. Identify loose files, confusing names, possible duplicate versions, and candidates for archiving, but do not treat matching names or older dates alone as reasons to delete anything.

Based on how this folder is actually used, propose a simple organization scheme. Use existing files as examples and show their exact locations before and after. Explain what should stay as it is and which moves might affect projects, applications, or file references.

First deliver the folder overview and organization plan in the conversation, clearly listing proposed moves, renames, and decisions I need to make. Wait for my confirmation before carrying out the plan.
